input:
Earlier scenes:
很久以前，古代的人很不知道什么植物能吃，也什么植物不能吃。所以很多人常常吃不安全的植物，吃不安全的植物对你的身体有坏处，很麻烦的情况。但是一个人，神农，要解决这个问题。他又聪明又努力，旅行很远找到很多植物。比方说，灵芝和夹竹桃。他一吃各种各样的植物就知道能不能吃这些植物。然后，神农写他的主意。他喜欢植物的味道，特别是花。神农遇到了一个黄色的花，一吃就觉得不舒服。

This scene:
发现了夹竹桃有毒。别人看到他，很快给他吃一个灵芝。神农一吃就觉得比较好。然后，他继续写他发现的信息。会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能不能吃。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 发现了夹竹桃有毒：it is unclear that夹竹桃refers to黄色的花
- 别人看到他：另外一个人，“别(的)” is for “a different type”, and “all else except the spoken one”, whereas “另外“ is for “addition in quantity”, and “another, the other”
- 会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能不能吃：也会告诉他的朋友哪一个植物能吃，哪个植物不能吃

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 比较好：好多了，比较 requires a stated comparison, while the intended meaning is that his condition improved after taking the medicine.
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 写他发现的信息：记下他发现的信息，记下 means to record information so it can be kept; bare 写 is not natural for recording discovered information in this context.
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 哪一个植物能不能吃：哪些植物能吃，哪些植物不能吃，do not combine a question word with an A-not-A question when stating general information; this version clearly contrasts edible and inedible plants.
4. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 别人看到他：一个穿着蓝色衣服的男人看到他，别人 distinguishes other people from the speaker and cannot introduce one specific new helper; at first mention, use a full noun phrase.
5. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 很快给他吃一个灵芝：很快给他吃了一个灵芝，use 了 after the completed action of giving him the medicine to eat.

items.reason: “觉得比较好” is acceptable here, even though “好多了” is a more natural way to emphasize improvement.
“写他发现的信息” is acceptable Chinese; “记下” is only a stylistic improvement.
A question word such as “哪一个” should not be combined with the A-not-A form “能不能” in this reported-information structure.
“别人” is not suitable for introducing one new helper here, while a full noun phrase such as “一个穿着蓝色衣服的男人” does introduce a specific person.
The feeding action is a completed narrative event, so it should take perfective “了”.
